vsm2.12:49.1: 7. Visavitā—“majesty”: not in PED; cf. passavati. Vism-mhṭ (p. 385) glosses with iddhiyā vividhānisaṃsa-pasavanāya. Cf. Dhs-a 109; Dhs-ṭ (p. 84) glosses thus visavitāyā ti arahatāya.
vsm2.12:53.3: 8. Further explanatory details are given in the commentary to the Iddhipāda Vibhaṅga.
vsm2.12:55.1: 9. Aneja (or aneñja)—“unperturbed”: form not in PED.
vsm2.12:60.2: 10. Aṅgīrasa—“the One with Radiant Limbs”: one of the epithets for the Buddha. Not in PED; see A III 239.
vsm2.12:64.2: 11. Dedication of what is to be given accompanied by pouring water over the hand.
vsm2.12:67.4: 12. “‘They become of the kinds desired’: they become whatever the kinds that were desired: for they come to possess as many varieties in appearance, etc., as it was wished they should have. But although they become manifold in this way by being made the object in different modes of appearance, nevertheless it is only a single resolution consciousness that occurs. This is its power. For it is like the single volition that produces a personality possessed of many different facets (see Ch. XIV, n. 14). And there it is the aspiration to become that is a condition for the differentiation in the kamma; and kamma-result is imponderable. And here too it is the preliminary-work consciousness that should be taken as a condition for the difference. And the field of supernormal power is imponderable too.” (Vism-mhṭ 390)
